Your eleven is solid at 60.8, rising to 69.0 with the armband on Haaland. He sits 0.3 clear of Salah and carries reasonable upside—a one-in-four chance of 10+—though he also has an 8% tail risk of returning 2 or fewer.

The model wants Wood out for Watkins, a free transfer that nets 6.4 points over the horizon with no hit taken. Watkins projects 6.4; Wood projects 4.2. Your bench is thin—Mykolenko at 3.1 is the only alternative with any weight—so the move also refreshes your forward line.

Triple Captain this week is worth 8.2 on Haaland, which assumes you keep him armband-favoured. That's a big swing, but it rests on the same captain logic you've already backed: he's your highest projection and the gap to second is small enough that variance matters more than it usually does. The chip amplifies both the upside and the tail.

You have three Arsenal players and two each from Liverpool and Manchester City. That's concentration worth noting if the fixtures turn, though it isn't flagged as a problem here.

Your team projects 69.0 points with Haaland captained. The only move on the table is Wood to Watkins, which nets 6.4 with no hit cost—a clean upgrade that pushes your horizon projection up. Triple Captain on Haaland would add 8.2 on top of his armband points, but that's a one-time gain and leaves you without the chip for later.

Haaland is a defensible captain: he's 0.3 clear of Salah and flagged for a ceiling game with a 25% chance of 10+. The downside is real though—he carries an 8% chance of returning 2 or fewer. Salah at 7.9 offers similar security without that tail risk, though fractionally lower upside.

Your structure leans heavy on two clubs. Arsenal supply three players in the eleven and Liverpool two, alongside two from Manchester City. That concentration works if those teams fire; it leaves you exposed if they don't.

The decision is whether to take Watkins now or wait. He's a straightforward gain either way—the question is whether you'd rather have the armband flexibility this week or cash the upgrade in while you have a free transfer.

Your eleven projects 60.8 points. The suggested move is to bring in Watkins for Wood, gaining 6.4 points at no cost—you have the transfer free. That takes you to 67.2 before any chip or captain choice.

Haaland wears the armband at 8.2 expected, 0.3 clear of Salah. The armband adds 8.2 to the baseline, putting you at 75.4. Haaland has an 8% chance of returning 2 or fewer and a 25% chance of 10 or more; Salah at 7.9 is a marginally closer thing, though the model prefers Haaland.

The alternative is to play Triple Captain this gameweek on Haaland, which the model values at 8.2 points gained. That would give you 75.4 as well, matching the armband play. The difference between them hinges on whether Haaland outperforms his projection by enough to make trebling worthwhile, and on your appetite for using the chip now rather than later.

Your bench is thin—Mykolenko projects 3.1, the rest well below 2—so this is a clean eleven with little flexibility mid-week. The move to Watkins is clear-cut if you're playing it straight; the chip decision is where your gameweek turns.
